browserCapability.blocker: No local browser backend was available to the in-app browser runtime.

cases.summary: Camera-off initial runtime, pre-consent model-load count, and pre-consent permission-request count were not observable without a local browser backend. Static defaults were not promoted to runtime pass evidence.
The deterministic adapter test observed one fake media request with video enabled and audio disabled. No physical device was addressed.
Synthetic UI rendering observed a named local preview, an Estimated expression state, and a checked reply-tone switch. Runtime revocation while capture remains active was not observed.

Fake media tests observed two synthetic tracks stopped on adapter stop, preview detachment, one track stopped on page hidden, sign-out ordering with camera stop before auth, and guest-expiry camera stop plus guest clear. User-stop, unmount, fatal-error, and pending-inference teardown were not independently observed.
The targeted suite did not instrument timer cancellation or concurrent inference count. Source control flow was not promoted to runtime pass evidence.

Synthetic tests observed remote model origin rejection before fake media request, no estimate fabrication for that rejection, unknown label fallback, low-confidence non-neutral fallback, and two-sample stability. Denied, unsupported, model-load error, no-face, and inference-error browser states were not independently observed end to end.

The camera-off synthetic UI fixture exposed an enabled text composer. Text continuation after denied, unsupported, model-failure, no-face, stop, hidden, sign-out, and expiry states was not observed in a browser.
No executed packet test covered a positive-text plus estimated-sad provider or reply fixture. Traceability mapping alone was not treated as behavioral evidence.
Dynamic network and browser-storage observation could not run without a local browser backend. No zero-egress or zero-persistence runtime claim is made.
